docs.title: MSF Laravel Notify
docs.text: msflib/notify is the notification package in the MSF Laravel ecosystem. It provides reusable notification primitives and Laravel integration points for downstream apps and packages that need consistent message delivery and event-driven communication patterns.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package provides:

  • Laravel service-provider integration
  • reusable notification primitives and helpers
  • package-level GraphQL or API integration when relevant
  • a shared notification foundation for the broader MSF stack

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• keep notification logic reusable and domain-aware
  • prefer package integration over app-specific wiring
  • keep examples aligned with the actual Laravel package metadata

docs.title: Package overview
docs.text: The msflib/notify package is designed to provide a shared notification layer for Laravel applications and package ecosystems. It follows the same MSF conventions as the rest of the Laravel packages: modular bootstrapping, consistent service-provider registration, and reusable domain-specific logic.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
This package is intended to cover:

  • notification domain registration and setup
  • Laravel bootstrapping and provider wiring
  • support for reusable messaging flows
  • integration with broader common and GraphQL conventions

docs.title: Expectation for downstream apps
docs.text:
The package should be included in Laravel apps through Composer and the Laravel auto-discovery or provider registration defined in composer.json.

"extra": {
  "laravel": {
    "providers": [
      "Msflib\\Notify\\MsfNotifyServiceProvider"
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use Msflib\Notify\NotificationChannel;

$channel = app(NotificationChannel::class);

The exact class names may vary by repo state, but the goal is a reusable notification abstraction that can be consumed consistently by multiple apps.

docs.title: Development guidance
docs.text:
• keep the package focused on notifications and message dispatch
  • prefer shared message abstractions over app-only conventions
  • document events and channels clearly for consumers
  • validate the package with the project test suite
